name: Parwal ki Mithai
instructions: 1. Peel the parwal, slice off the ends, and make a slit lengthwise to carefully scoop out the seeds.
2. Blanch the parwals in boiling water for 5 minutes, then drain.
3. Prepare a sugar syrup (one-string consistency) and boil the parwals in it for 10-12 minutes until translucent; let them cool.
4. In a pan, roast the khoya until soft, add sugar, cardamom powder, and dry fruits, stirring until it thickens into a stuffing.
5. Gently stuff each parwal with the prepared khoya mixture.
6. Garnish with slivered nuts and serve chilled.
description: A celebrated sweet from Bihar, Parwal ki Mithai turns a humble vegetable into a royal dessert. It is traditionally prepared during festivals and weddings, showcasing the creative culinary heritage of the region where seasonal produce is transformed into sophisticated confections.
